architecture.mechanism: Clearance between the flat-faced follower and its guides produces impact and friction at the cam-follower-guide contacts, driving non-linear (potentially chaotic) follower motion that raises cyclic contact stress and promotes surface fatigue spalling.
architecture.intervention: Replace or re-bore the follower guides to a controlled, reduced clearance (and add lubrication/retention to the guide and cam-follower interface) while retaining the certified cam profile and the 16 mm follower class, so the follower tracks the cam with minimal impact and friction.
architecture.expected_effect: Lower peak contact stress and fewer high-amplitude impact stress cycles at 420 cycles per minute, extending follower spalling life well beyond 6-9 weeks and cutting metal debris release into the food-contact zone, with maintenance intervals at or under once per week.
architecture.falsification_test: Mount a high-resolution optical marker on the follower stem, record follower y-displacement at 420 cpm before and after the clearance reduction, and compare impact severity (acceleration spikes) and the largest Lyapunov exponent; the mechanism is falsified if the reduced-clearance run shows no decrease in impact spikes or chaotic signature.
